segments.script: First, meaning. I read “How very ill Eliza Bennet looks this morning, Mr. Darcy” slowly and put it in my own words: Miss Bingley tells Darcy that Elizabeth looks ill, brown and coarse this morning. Next, craft. I notice the jealous exaggeration aimed at Darcy, not at Elizabeth. The strongest word is “ill”: the word is meant to make Darcy see Elizabeth as unattractive. Then, effect. Why does Miss Bingley attack Elizabeth's looks in front of Darcy? My answer: Her spite backfires: Darcy answers that Elizabeth is one of the handsomest women he knows, which shows that his feelings have only grown.
